name: Jon Stein
current_role: Founder and chairman, Betterment (CEO 2008–Dec 2020); angel investor/advisor
profile: American fintech entrepreneur (Harvard BA, Columbia MBA) who founded Betterment, the pioneering robo-advisor, in 2008 after ~4 years at First Manhattan Consulting Group. He was CEO until December 2020, when ex-Viacom COO Sarah Levy succeeded him; he remains founder/chairman and advises and invests in startups.
interesting_fact: He launched Betterment on stage at TechCrunch's 2008 Startup Battlefield in the middle of the financial crisis, betting big banks would be distracted by lost trust; he was named to Fortune's 40 Under 40 in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: For the TechCrunch launch pitch he memorized his speech and practiced it about 50 times (he says he never memorized a speech again), overdressed, and got teased by Michael Arrington about his tie; Betterment's servers went live for the first time that day.
notes: Current day-to-day activities after stepping down as CEO are not well documented; a profile site mentions a new venture called 'Warmer' but this is unverified. In 2020 he said his next startup would not be in finance.

name: Rafael Lopez
current_role: Listed as a ZenBusiness founder/'Product Director' on an insider-data aggregator; not named on ZenBusiness's current leadership page
profile: Rafael Lopez is named as one of several ZenBusiness co-founders (alongside Ross Buhrdorf, Shanaz Hemmati, JC Glancy and Art Flores) in a secondary source and as a founder/Product Director on MarketScreener. ZenBusiness, an Austin-based small-business formation and compliance platform founded in 2015, was valued around $1.7B. No independent biography was found.
interesting_fact: ZenBusiness is a public benefit corporation (ZenBusiness PBC) in Austin that helps small-business owners form LLCs, stay compliant and manage finances; a 2025 CNBC piece described it as a $1.7 billion startup.
notes: Very low public profile; company's official founder list (website, Wikipedia) names only Buhrdorf and Hemmati. 'Rafael Lopez' is a common name - verify identity (e.g. via the Forbes listing) before outreach. Best route is via ZenBusiness press.

name: Thomas France
current_role: Co-founder of Ledger (board advisor per profile aggregators); founder/managing partner of Cygni Capital (crypto/trust-tech VC)
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded Ledger, the Paris-based maker of crypto hardware wallets, in 2014 (Ledger later raised $380M in 2021 at unicorn valuation). Earlier he co-founded the shopping app Prixing. After stepping back from operations around 2019 he co-founded Cygni Capital, investing in blockchain, privacy and AI, and is an active angel investor.
interesting_fact: Ledger, which he co-founded in 2014, became one of France's best-known crypto unicorns, building secure hardware wallets for digital assets and raising $380M in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2014, with Eric Larcheveque, he opened La Maison du Bitcoin on rue du Caire in Paris, a physical venue for training in and buying cryptocurrencies, often described as Europe's first bitcoin space and a precursor to Ledger.
notes: Ledger press email is for the company, where he is no longer an operator. Cygni Capital has no confirmed official website; dates from aggregator profiles (MarketScreener, Dealroom) are inconsistent. Low media profile; appeared on the 'Can't Be Done' podcast (ep. 58).

name: Liran Antebi
current_role: Co-founder and (founding) Chief Architect, Orca Security; current title not confirmed
profile: Israeli software engineer who co-founded cloud-security company Orca Security in 2019 with Avi Shua, Gil Geron and Matan Ben Gur, all Check Point Software veterans. Orca's agentless 'SideScanning' cloud-security platform raised large rounds and reached a ~$1.8B valuation. Antebi keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: Orca was founded by a team of former Check Point executives and architects; Antebi and Matan Ben Gur were the founding 'chief architects' when the company emerged from stealth with a $6.5M seed round in 2019.

public_contacts.value: Inkhouse on behalf of Orca Security: orcasecurity@inkhouse.com (per a 2026 Orca press release; verify)

notes: Not listed on Orca's current leadership page (orca.security/about), so he may have stepped back from an executive role. No interviews found. Aggregators claim ~16 years at Check Point before Orca, unverified by a primary source. Route via Orca press.

name: Harry Kim
current_role: Co-founder, Sendbird (listed as Founder/CTO on Y Combinator; some profiles say Chief Architect)
profile: Korean-born engineer who co-founded Sendbird with CEO John S. Kim, Brandon Jeon and Forest Lee; it went through Y Combinator (W16), moved HQ to San Mateo and became a chat/messaging API unicorn (~$1B+ valuation in 2021). Sendbird is now pivoting to AI customer-service agents (Delight.ai). Per profiles he was earlier technical director at Paprika Lab (acquired by GREE).
interesting_fact: Sendbird began as a pivot: the team was building 'Smile Mom', an app to connect nearby mothers, couldn't find a good off-the-shelf chat tool, built their own, and friends kept asking to use it - so they turned the chat engine into the company.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Not to be confused with John S. Kim (CEO). Earlier career details (Paprika Lab, GREE Korea, Wisenut, Monash University) come only from aggregator profiles. No verified Sendbird press email found; a past release listed Moore Communications as PR contact.

name: Gilles Wainrib
current_role: Co-founder of Owkin (Chief Scientific Officer since 2016 per profiles; current title unconfirmed)
profile: French applied mathematician and machine-learning researcher who co-founded Owkin in Paris in 2016 with haematologist Thomas Clozel. Owkin uses AI and privacy-preserving (federated) learning on hospital data for drug discovery and diagnostics, became a unicorn in 2021 after a Sanofi investment, and now builds agentic AI for biology (K Navigator, K Pro). He came from academia (Stanford postdoc, assistant professor).
interesting_fact: Owkin's founding idea was to unlock insights from vast amounts of patient data held in hospitals and research centers 'in a privacy-preserving and secure way' - Owkin describes Wainrib as a pioneer of machine learning in biology.
deep_cut_fact: Before Owkin he was a mathematical neuroscientist: with Jonathan Touboul (Collège de France team) he co-authored work on bifurcations of stochastic differential equations and macroscopic limits of large stochastic neural networks.

public_contacts.value: alistair.jennings@owkin.com (international media; page's mailto link points to michelle.shearly@owkin.com)

notes: Low-profile scientist co-founder; Thomas Clozel is Owkin's public face. Press contacts on Owkin's press kit change often - check the latest release. Education (Ecole Polytechnique) per TheOrg, not independently verified.

name: Kent Wakeford
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Form Bio (computational biology spinout of Colossal); co-founder and former COO of Colossal Biosciences
profile: Serial tech entrepreneur who co-founded de-extinction company Colossal Biosciences (with Ben Lamm and George Church) and served as its COO, then became co-founder and co-CEO of Form Bio, the computational-biology software company Colossal spun out in 2022. Earlier he co-founded Integral Ad Science (NASDAQ: IAS) and was COO of game maker Kabam.
interesting_fact: Colossal, which he co-founded, aims to 'de-extinct' the woolly mammoth, thylacine and dodo; it hit unicorn status with a $150M Series B in 2023, and Form Bio commercialises the software built for that work.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech he was a media/gaming tech builder: he is a co-inventor on more than 85 patents covering virtual reality and streaming technology, and co-founded four software companies including Integral Ad Science.
notes: Dallas-based. For outreach, Form Bio is his current company; Colossal press is agency-run (R&CPMK, Zeno, The 10 Group). Some aggregators list him as special advisor to Colossal's CEO. A Dec 2025 Colossal Foundation release reportedly lists Emily@colossal.com as media contact, but this could not be verified directly.

name: Alexander Zosel
current_role: Co-founder of Volocopter (eVTOL air-taxi pioneer, Bruchsal); current role unconfirmed after Volocopter's 2025 acquisition by Diamond Aircraft
profile: German serial entrepreneur (civil-engineering studies) who co-founded e-volo/Volocopter in Karlsruhe in 2011 with Stephan Wolf, pioneering electric multicopter air taxis and serving in roles including managing director and technical/marketing lead. Volocopter raised hundreds of millions, then filed for insolvency in Dec 2024; its assets were bought by Wanfeng's Diamond Aircraft in March 2025.
interesting_fact: On 30 March 2016 Zosel personally piloted the first manned flight of the 18-rotor Volocopter VC200, saying: 'It is definitely a sublime feeling to lift off, fly the first few meters.'
deep_cut_fact: In 1981, aged 15, he and friends built one of Germany's first skateboard halfpipes; he developed his first patent while still a civil-engineering student.
notes: Current activities after the Volocopter insolvency/Diamond takeover are undocumented; avoid dwelling on the insolvency. Has given interviews (tech.eu, dronebelow, re:publica 2018 speaker). No published personal or office contact found.

name: Ikenna Okezie
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and director, Somatus (value-based kidney care, Tysons/McLean, Virginia)
profile: Nigerian-born physician-executive (Yale economics BA; Harvard MD/MBA) who led DaVita Kidney Care's Mid-Atlantic market (2010-15) before co-founding Somatus in 2016 with investor Anthony Welters. Somatus manages kidney (and now heart) care for 500,000+ patients across all 50 states and was valued at about $2.5B after a $325M Series E in 2022.
interesting_fact: He started Somatus because he 'wanted to start a business that focused on delaying kidney disease progression and keeping people as healthy as possible', rather than only treating patients once they reach dialysis.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Nigeria and raised in Detroit and Chicago, he studied economics at Yale before earning a dual MD/MBA at Harvard with concentrations in finance and entrepreneurship; his father and elder brother are also physicians.

public_contacts.value: media@somatus.com (listed on syndicated Somatus press releases; not confirmed on somatus.com)

notes: Fairly media-friendly (CNBC Disruptor 50 profile, Nigerian press). Sits on boards of the National Kidney Foundation/ASN per profiles. Physician-father detail is from Nairametrics profile (https://nairametrics.com/2024/05/07/meet-ikenna-okezie-brain-behind-2-5-billion-kidney-care-company-in-united-states/).

name: Glen Tullman
current_role: Founder & CEO, Transcarent; managing partner, 7wireVentures; co-founder, Tullman Family Office
profile: Chicago-area serial healthcare entrepreneur: CEO of Allscripts for ~15 years (1997-2012), then founded Livongo (2014), which IPO'd in 2019 and merged with Teladoc in a deal valued at $18.5B in 2020. In 2021 he founded Transcarent, an AI-powered health and care platform for employers and health plans, and invests via 7wireVentures and 62 Ventures (2024).
interesting_fact: He has invested in or co-founded more than 20 businesses, including SoCore Energy, a commercial solar installer later bought by Edison International - a clean-energy angle beyond his healthcare fame.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from Bucknell (economics and psychology, 1981) he spent a year in Oxford, England studying social anthropology; his first long stint was ~10 years at Certified Collateral Corporation (later CCC Information Services), rising to president and COO.
notes: Very media-accessible; author of 'On Our Terms: Empowering the New Health Consumer', RFK Ripple of Hope Award 2019. Good podcast guest candidate. Wikipedia notes a possible COI contributor, so double-check details.

name: Nathan Mintz
current_role: Co-founder of Epirus (directed-energy/high-power-microwave defense company, Torrance CA); not listed on Epirus's current leadership page, so current role unconfirmed
profile: Nathan Mintz is listed as a founder of Epirus, the Los Angeles-area defense-tech startup behind Leonidas, a solid-state high-power-microwave system used to disable drone swarms. Epirus raised $70M (Series B, 2020), $200M (Series C, 2022) and a $250M Series D (March 2025) to scale Leonidas production. His personal background could not be independently verified in this pass.
interesting_fact: Epirus's Leonidas high-power-microwave system was selected for the U.S. Department of War directed-energy pilot program, and the company's $250M Series D in 2025 went to scaling its production for counter-drone defense.
notes: Research cut short by a web-search quota; Mintz's biography, current role and status were not verified - needs a follow-up pass. Epirus press contact is for the company, which he may no longer run day to day.
